1	# CoolStore Monolith
2	
3	A Java EE 7 e-commerce application deployed on Oracle WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4. Uses an embedded H2 database — no external database required.
4	
5	## Prerequisites
6	
7	- Java 8 (JDK)
8	- Maven 3.x
9	- Podman (with a running machine) and podman-compose
10	
11	## Download the WebLogic Container Image
12	
13	The application runs on Oracle WebLogic Server. The container image must be pulled from Oracle Container Registry, which requires a free Oracle account and an auth token.
14	
15	A helper script is provided to handle login and download:
16	
17	```bash
18	./download-container-image.sh
19	```
20	
21	The script will prompt for your Oracle credentials. Use your **auth token** as the password (not your Oracle account password).
22	
23	To generate an auth token:
24	
25	1. Sign in at https://cloud.oracle.com
26	2. Click your profile icon (top-right) and select **User Settings**
27	3. Under **Auth Tokens**, click **Generate Token**
28	4. Copy the token immediately — it is only shown once
29	
30	You also need to accept the WebLogic license (one-time):
31	
32	1. Go to https://container-registry.oracle.com
33	2. Sign in, search for `weblogic`
34	3. Click **middleware/weblogic**, then **Continue** and accept the license
35	
36	## Project Structure
37	
38	```
39	├── pom.xml                     # Maven build (produces ROOT.war)
40	├── docker-compose.yml          # Podman/Docker compose for local dev
41	├── weblogic-config/            # WebLogic domain and resource setup scripts
42	│   ├── create-domain.py        # WLST: creates the WebLogic domain
43	│   ├── configure-resources.py  # WLST: configures JDBC (H2) and JMS resources
44	│   ├── deploy-app.py           # WLST: deploys the WAR to the server
45	│   └── entrypoint.sh           # Container entrypoint (orchestrates all of the above)
46	└── src/
47	    ├── main/java/              # Application source code
48	    ├── main/resources/
49	    │   └── META-INF/
50	    │       ├── persistence.xml # JPA config (EclipseLink + H2)
51	    │       └── import.sql      # Seed data loaded on startup
52	    └── main/webapp/            # Web frontend + deployment descriptors
53	```
54	
55	## Build
56	
57	```bash
58	mvn clean package
59	```
60	
61	This produces `target/ROOT.war`.
62	
63	## Run Locally with Podman
64	
65	### Start
66	
67	```bash
68	mvn clean package && podman-compose up
69	```
70	
71	First startup takes approximately 5 minutes (domain creation, resource configuration, app deployment). Subsequent starts are faster because the domain is persisted in a named volume.
72	
73	Once you see `WebLogic Admin Server Ready!` in the logs, the application is available at:
74	
75	| URL | Description |
76	|---|---|
77	| http://localhost:8080/ | Web storefront |
78	| http://localhost:8080/services/products | Products REST API |
79	| http://localhost:8080/services/cart/{cartId} | Shopping cart API |
80	| http://localhost:8080/services/orders | Orders REST API |
81	| http://localhost:8080/console | WebLogic Admin Console |
82	
83	Admin console credentials: `weblogic` / `welcome1`
84	
85	### Stop
86	
87	```bash
88	podman-compose down
89	```
90	
91	### Full Reset
92	
93	Wipe the WebLogic domain and H2 database to start completely fresh:
94	
95	```bash
96	podman-compose down
97	podman pod rm -af && podman rm -af
98	podman volume rm coolstore_weblogic_domain coolstore_h2_data
99	```
100	
101	### View Logs
102	
103	```bash
104	podman logs -f coolstore-weblogic
105	```
106	
107	## Build a Container Image
108	
109	Create a self-contained image with the WAR baked in:
110	
111	```bash
112	mvn clean package
113	
114	podman build -t coolstore-weblogic:latest -f Containerfile .
115	```
116	
117	Using this `Containerfile`:
118	
119	```dockerfile
120	FROM container-registry.oracle.com/middleware/weblogic:12.2.1.4-dev
121	
122	COPY weblogic-config/ /u01/config/
123	COPY target/ROOT.war /u01/app/ROOT.war
124	COPY target/ROOT/WEB-INF/lib/h2-1.4.200.jar /u01/app/h2-1.4.200.jar
125	
126	CMD ["/bin/bash", "/u01/config/entrypoint.sh"]
127	```
128	
129	Run the built image standalone (no compose needed):
130	
131	```bash
132	podman run -d --name coolstore \
133	  -p 8080:8080 \
134	  -e ADMIN_USERNAME=weblogic \
135	  -e ADMIN_PASSWORD=welcome1 \
136	  -e DOMAIN_NAME=coolstore_domain \
137	  coolstore-weblogic:latest
138	```
139	
140	## Push to a Private Quay Repository
141	
142	Tag and push the image to your Quay registry:
143	
144	```bash
145	# Log in to Quay (once)
146	podman login quay.io
147	
148	# Tag the image
149	podman tag coolstore-weblogic:latest quay.io/<your-org>/coolstore-weblogic:latest
150	
151	# Push
152	podman push quay.io/<your-org>/coolstore-weblogic:latest
153	```
154	
155	To use a specific version tag:
156	
157	```bash
158	podman tag coolstore-weblogic:latest quay.io/<your-org>/coolstore-weblogic:1.0.0
159	podman push quay.io/<your-org>/coolstore-weblogic:1.0.0
160	```
161	
162	Pulling from the private repo on another machine:
163	
164	```bash
165	podman login quay.io
166	podman pull quay.io/<your-org>/coolstore-weblogic:latest
167	```
168	
169	## Deploy to OpenShift
170	
171	A deployment script is provided that builds the image, pushes it to a registry, and creates all OpenShift resources (Deployment, Service, Route with TLS).
172	
173	### Prerequisites
174	
175	- `oc` CLI, logged into an OpenShift cluster (`oc login <cluster-url>`)
176	- Podman
177	- Access to a container registry that OpenShift can pull from
178	
179	### Using the OpenShift internal registry
180	
181	```bash
182	./deploy-openshift.sh
183	```
184	
185	The script auto-detects the internal registry route. If the route is not exposed, enable it first:
186	
187	```bash
188	oc patch configs.imageregistry.operator.openshift.io/cluster \
189	  --type merge -p '{"spec":{"defaultRoute":true}}'
190	```
191	
192	### Using Quay or another external registry
193	
194	```bash
195	./deploy-openshift.sh --registry quay.io/<your-org>
196	```
197	
198	Make sure you are logged into the registry (`podman login quay.io`) and that OpenShift has a pull secret configured for it.
199	
200	### Options
201	
202	| Flag | Description | Default |
203	|---|---|---|
204	| `--registry <url>` | Container registry to push to | OpenShift internal |
205	| `--project <name>` | OpenShift project/namespace | `coolstore` |
206	| `--tag <tag>` | Image tag | `latest` |
207	
208	### What the script creates
209	
210	| Resource | Name | Description |
211	|---|---|---|
212	| Secret | `coolstore-credentials` | WebLogic admin username and password |
213	| Deployment | `coolstore` | Single replica, 2-4 GB memory, readiness/liveness probes |
214	| Service | `coolstore` | ClusterIP on port 8080 |
215	| Route | `coolstore` | TLS edge termination with HTTPS redirect |
216	
217	### After deployment
218	
219	```bash
220	# Check pod status
221	oc get pods -l app=coolstore
222	
223	# Follow logs
224	oc logs -f deployment/coolstore
225	
226	# Get the application URL
227	oc get route coolstore -o jsonpath='https://{.spec.host}{"\n"}'
228	
229	# Tear down everything
230	oc delete project coolstore
231	```
232	
233	The first pod startup takes approximately 5 minutes while WebLogic creates the domain, configures resources, and deploys the WAR.
234	
235	## REST API Examples
236	
237	```bash
238	# List all products
239	curl http://localhost:8080/services/products
240	
241	# Get shopping cart
242	curl http://localhost:8080/services/cart/123
243	
244	# Add an item to cart (itemId=329299, quantity=1)
245	curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/services/cart/123/329299/1
246	
247	# Checkout
248	curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/services/cart/checkout/123
249	
250	# List orders
251	curl http://localhost:8080/services/orders
252	```
253	
254	## Technology Stack
255	
256	| Component | Technology |
257	|---|---|
258	| Runtime | Oracle WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4 |
259	| Language | Java 8, Java EE 7 |
260	| JPA Provider | EclipseLink 2.6 (WebLogic built-in) |
261	| Database | H2 1.4.200 (embedded) |
262	| JAX-RS | Jersey 2.x (WebLogic built-in) |
263	| Messaging | WebLogic JMS |
264	| Frontend | AngularJS + PatternFly |
265

1	# CoolStore Monolith — Architecture
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	CoolStore is a Java EE 7 e-commerce monolith deployed on Oracle WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4. It exposes a REST API consumed by an AngularJS/PatternFly single-page application. All business logic, messaging, and persistence run inside a single WAR deployed to one WebLogic Admin Server.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Technology Stack
10	
11	| Layer | Technology |
12	|---|---|
13	| Runtime | Oracle WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4 |
14	| Language | Java 8, Java EE 7 |
15	| Build | Maven 3.x → `ROOT.war` |
16	| Persistence | JPA (EclipseLink 2.6, built-in to WebLogic) |
17	| Database | H2 1.4.200 (embedded, file-backed) |
18	| JAX-RS | Jersey 2.x (built-in to WebLogic) |
19	| Messaging | WebLogic JMS |
20	| Frontend | AngularJS + PatternFly |
21	| CDI | Weld (built-in to WebLogic) |
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Package Structure
26	
27	```
28	com.redhat.coolstore
29	├── model/          — JPA entities and domain DTOs
30	├── persistence/    — CDI producers (EntityManager, Logger)
31	├── rest/           — JAX-RS endpoints
32	├── service/        — EJB business logic and MDBs
33	└── utils/          — JSON transformers, CDI producers, startup listener
34	```
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Application Layers
39	
40	### REST Layer (`com.redhat.coolstore.rest`)
41	
42	All endpoints are mounted under `/services/`.
43	
44	| Class | Path | Methods | Notes |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| `RestApplication` | `/services` | — | JAX-RS `Application` config |
47	| `ProductEndpoint` | `/services/products` | `GET` | Lists catalog products |
48	| `CartEndpoint` | `/services/cart/{cartId}` | `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` | `@SessionScoped`; manages cart lifecycle |
49	| `OrderEndpoint` | `/services/orders` | `GET` | Lists persisted orders |
50	
51	`CartEndpoint` is `@SessionScoped` so each HTTP session maintains its own cart reference.
52	
53	### Service Layer (`com.redhat.coolstore.service`)
54	
55	| Class | EJB Type | Responsibility |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `CatalogService` | `@Stateless` | JPA queries against `PRODUCT_CATALOG` and inventory tables |
58	| `ProductService` | `@Stateless` | Translates `CatalogItemEntity` to `Product` DTO |
59	| `ShoppingCartService` | `@Stateful` | Holds cart state per session; orchestrates pricing, promotions, shipping |
60	| `ShippingService` | `@Stateless @Remote` | Calculates shipping cost and insurance by cart total thresholds |
61	| `PromoService` | `@ApplicationScoped` | Applies item-level and shipping-level promotions (hard-coded rule set) |
62	| `OrderService` | `@Stateless` | Persists `Order` entities via JPA |
63	| `ShoppingCartOrderProcessor` | `@Stateless` | JMS producer — serialises cart to JSON and publishes to `orders` topic |
64	| `OrderServiceMDB` | `@MessageDriven` | JMS consumer — deserialises order, saves it, updates inventory |
65	| `InventoryNotificationMDB` | `@MessageDriven` | JMS consumer — checks inventory thresholds, logs supplier warnings |
66	
67	### Model Layer (`com.redhat.coolstore.model`)
68	
69	| Class | Type | Notes |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| `CatalogItemEntity` | JPA `@Entity` | `PRODUCT_CATALOG` table; 1:1 with `InventoryEntity` |
72	| `InventoryEntity` | JPA `@Entity` | Tracks stock quantity |
73	| `Product` | DTO | Flattened view of `CatalogItemEntity` for the REST API |
74	| `ShoppingCart` | POJO | Aggregates `ShoppingCartItem` list, totals, and savings fields |
75	| `ShoppingCartItem` | POJO | Line item: product, price, quantity, promo savings |
76	| `Order` / `OrderItem` | JPA entities | Persisted after checkout |
77	| `Promotion` | POJO | Item ID + percent-off discount |
78	
79	---
80	
81	## Data Flow
82	
83	### Browsing Products
84	
85	```
86	Browser → GET /services/products
87	       → ProductEndpoint
88	       → ProductService.getProducts()
89	       → CatalogService.getCatalogItems()  [JPA → H2]
90	       → Transformers.toProduct()
91	       ← JSON list of products
92	```
93	
94	### Add to Cart and Checkout
95	
96	```
97	Browser → POST /services/cart/{cartId}/{itemId}/{qty}
98	        → CartEndpoint.add()
99	        → ShoppingCartService
100	            → ProductService (fetch product)
101	            → PromoService.applyCartItemPromotions()
102	            → ShippingService (JNDI: ejb/ShippingService)
103	        ← Updated ShoppingCart JSON
104	
105	Browser → POST /services/cart/checkout/{cartId}
106	        → CartEndpoint.checkout()
107	        → ShoppingCartService.checkOutShoppingCart()
108	        → ShoppingCartOrderProcessor.process()
109	            → JMS publish to jms/topic/orders (JSON-encoded order)
110	        ← Empty cart JSON
111	```
112	
113	### Order Processing (Async via JMS)
114	
115	```
116	JMS Topic: jms/topic/orders
117	    ├── OrderServiceMDB.onMessage()
118	    │       → Transformers.jsonToOrder()
119	    │       → OrderService.save()           [JPA → H2]
120	    │       → CatalogService.updateInventoryItems()  [JPA → H2]
121	    │
122	    └── InventoryNotificationMDB.onMessage()
123	            → Checks if inventory < 50 (LOW_THRESHOLD)
124	            → Logs supplier warning if below threshold
125	```
126	
127	---
128	
129	## WebLogic Resources
130	
131	Configured via WLST Python scripts at container startup:
132	
133	| Resource | Type | JNDI Name | Details |
134	|---|---|---|---|
135	| `CoolstoreDS` | JDBC DataSource | `jdbc/CoolstoreDS` | H2 file DB at `/u01/data/coolstoredb`; pool 5–50 connections |
136	| `CoolstoreJMSServer` | JMS Server | — | Targeted to AdminServer |
137	| `CoolstoreJMSModule` | JMS Module | — | Contains the topic |
138	| `OrdersTopic` | JMS Topic | `jms/topic/orders` | Used by both MDBs and the order processor |
139	| Connection Factory | (WebLogic default) | `weblogic.jms.ConnectionFactory` | No custom factory needed |
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Promotion Rules
144	
145	`PromoService` (application-scoped, in-memory) implements two rules:
146	
147	- **Item promotion**: item `329299` gets 25% off.
148	- **Shipping promotion**: orders with item total ≥ $75 receive free shipping.
149	
150	Rules are hard-coded. No database or external configuration is involved.
151	
152	**Shipping tiers** (calculated by `ShippingService`):
153	
154	| Cart Total | Shipping Cost |
155	|---|---|
156	| $0 – $25 | $2.99 |
157	| $25 – $50 | $4.99 |
158	| $50 – $75 | $6.99 |
159	| $75 – $100 | $8.99 |
160	| $100 – $10,000 | $10.99 |
161	
162	Orders ≥ $25 also add a shipping insurance charge (2%, 1.5%, or 1% depending on total).
163	
164	---
165	
166	## Frontend
167	
168	The UI lives in `src/main/webapp/app/`:
169	
170	- **AngularJS** SPA with PatternFly CSS.
171	- `app.js` — module and routing.
172	- `controllers/controllers.js` — view logic.
173	- `directives/header.js` — shared header component.
174	- Product images bundled as static assets.
175	- `keycloak.json` present for optional SSO integration (Keycloak realm config in `realm-export.json`).
176	
177	---
178	
179	## Container and Deployment
180	
181	### Local Development (Podman Compose)
182	
183	```
184	podman-compose up
185	```
186	
187	- WebLogic image: `container-registry.oracle.com/middleware/weblogic:12.2.1.4-dev`
188	- Port `8080` exposed for admin console and application.
189	- Named volumes: `weblogic_domain` (domain persistence), `h2_data` (database files).
190	- Memory: 2–4 GB.
191	
192	### Container Startup Sequence (`entrypoint.sh`)
193	
194	1. **Create domain** — `create-domain.py` (WLST offline mode) if domain does not exist.
195	2. **Start AdminServer** — `startWebLogic.sh` in background; waits up to 180 s for `RUNNING` state.
196	3. **Configure resources** — `configure-resources.py` (WLST online) — JDBC and JMS; writes a flag file to skip on subsequent starts.
197	4. **Deploy WAR** — `deploy-app.py` deploys `ROOT.war`.
198	5. **Tail logs** — keeps the container alive.
199	
200	### OpenShift Deployment (`deploy-openshift.sh`)
201	
202	| Resource | Name | Details |
203	|---|---|---|
204	| Secret | `coolstore-credentials` | WebLogic admin username and password |
205	| Deployment | `coolstore` | Single replica, 2–4 GB memory, readiness/liveness probes |
206	| Service | `coolstore` | ClusterIP on port 8080 |
207	| Route | `coolstore` | TLS edge termination, HTTPS redirect |
208	
209	Use `--registry` flag to push to an external registry (e.g., Quay) instead of the OpenShift internal registry.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## Exception Handling Practices
214	
215	### Current Patterns
216	
217	The application has no centralised exception handling. Each layer handles (or propagates) errors differently:
218	
219	**REST layer — unchecked propagation**
220	
221	`CartEndpoint` declares `throws Exception` on mutation methods (`add`, `set`, `delete`). When `ShoppingCartService.priceShoppingCart` throws, the endpoint re-throws the raw exception after rolling back the cart item:
222	
223	```java
224	// CartEndpoint.java
225	try {
226	    shoppingCartService.priceShoppingCart(cart);
227	    cart.setShoppingCartItemList(dedupeCartItems(...));
228	} catch (Exception ex) {
229	    cart.removeShoppingCartItem(sci);
230	    throw ex;   // propagates as HTTP 500 with no structured body
231	}
232	```
233	
234	There is no `@ExceptionMapper` or `Response` wrapper, so any unhandled exception becomes an unstructured HTTP 500 response.
235	
236	**Service layer — checked exceptions wrapped as `RuntimeException`**
237	
238	JNDI lookup failures in `ShoppingCartService` and JMS failures in `OrderServiceMDB` are caught and re-thrown as unchecked exceptions, letting the EJB container handle transaction rollback:
239	
240	```java
241	// ShoppingCartService.java
242	} catch (NamingException e) {
243	    throw new RuntimeException(e);  // triggers EJB TX rollback
244	}
245	
246	// OrderServiceMDB.java
247	} catch (JMSException e) {
248	    throw new RuntimeException(e);  // triggers MDB redelivery by JMS provider
249	}
250	```
251	
252	**MDB layer — swallowed JMS exception**
253	
254	`InventoryNotificationMDB` catches `JMSException` and prints to `System.err` without re-throwing, which suppresses MDB redelivery:
255	
256	```java
257	// InventoryNotificationMDB.java
258	} catch (JMSException jmse) {
259	    System.err.println("An exception occurred: " + jmse.getMessage());
260	    // exception is swallowed — message will NOT be redelivered
261	}
262	```
263	
264	**Data layer — silent null propagation**
265	
266	`Transformers.toProduct` logs a warning when inventory is null but returns a partial `Product` object. Callers receive a product with zero quantity and no location rather than an error signal:
267	
268	```java
269	// Transformers.java
270	} else {
271	    log.warning("Inventory for " + entity.getName() + " unknown and missing");
272	    // prod.quantity stays 0, prod.location/link stay null
273	}
274	```
275	
276	### Logging
277	
278	Logging is inconsistent across the codebase:
279	
280	| Location | Mechanism | Level used |
281	|---|---|---|
282	| `CatalogService`, `ShoppingCartService`, `ShoppingCartOrderProcessor` | CDI-injected `java.util.logging.Logger` | `INFO` |
283	| `Transformers` | Static `java.util.logging.Logger` | `WARNING` |
284	| `OrderServiceMDB` | `System.out.println` | — |
285	| `InventoryNotificationMDB` | `System.out.println` / `System.err.println` | — |
286	| `StartupListener` | CDI-injected `Logger` | `INFO` |
287	
288	MDB classes use `System.out`/`System.err` directly instead of the injected logger used elsewhere in the service layer.
289	
290	### Known Gaps
291	
292	| Gap | Location | Impact |
293	|---|---|---|
294	| No JAX-RS `ExceptionMapper` | REST layer | Unhandled exceptions return raw HTTP 500 with a WebLogic stack trace body |
295	| `JMSException` swallowed | `InventoryNotificationMDB` | Failed inventory checks are lost; no redelivery, no dead-letter handling |
296	| `throws Exception` on REST methods | `CartEndpoint` | Overly broad contract; any downstream failure leaks as an untyped 500 |
297	| Null inventory silently ignored | `Transformers.toProduct` | Callers cannot distinguish "product has zero stock" from "inventory data missing" |
298	| No JNDI lookup retry | `ShoppingCartService` | A transient JNDI failure aborts the checkout with no fallback |
299	
300	---
301	
302	## Key Design Characteristics
303	
304	- **Single-process monolith**: all services, REST endpoints, JMS consumers, and the database run in one JVM inside a single WebLogic Admin Server.
305	- **Stateful session cart**: `ShoppingCartService` is a `@Stateful` EJB; cart state lives in the EJB container tied to the HTTP session.
306	- **Async order processing via JMS**: checkout is decoupled from order persistence — the cart endpoint returns immediately after publishing to the topic.
307	- **Embedded database**: H2 in file mode eliminates an external database dependency; the file is stored in a named volume for persistence across container restarts.
308	- **No external auth dependency at runtime**: Keycloak integration files are present but the application does not enforce authentication at the REST layer — auth is optional/configurable.
309

A code knowledge graph built for LLM agents
Usage: rgctl [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
Lifecycle:
  discover      Index and analyze a codebase
  status        Session graph status (snapshot presence, digest, node/edge counts, source staleness; no rediscover)
  update        Incremental structural graph update for changed files (not a full discover / analysis rebuild)
  watch         Watch the repo and apply incremental graph updates on save (`notify`, default 25ms debounce)
  merge         Merge multiple discovered repos, resolving parked cross-repo relations
  serve         Serve the universe dashboard and GQL query API over HTTP
  diff          Diff two columnar graph snapshots (cold diff profiling / compare path)

Query:
  find          Find symbols by name/type over the mmap graph index (no GQL)
  callers       Incoming CALLS neighbors for a symbol
  callees       Outgoing CALLS neighbors for a symbol
  relations     Typed edge traversal; omit SYMBOL for seedless set-wide scan
  inventory     Aggregate symbol/edge counts (includes zero-count schema kinds for type/edge)
  gql           Experimental graph query language — prefer `find` / `callers` / `relations` / `inventory` for common queries

Analysis:
  blast-radius  Macro impact / blast radius for a symbol
  slice         Line-level program slice or taint trace (builds & caches single-function CFG/PDG lazily on demand)
  taint         Sink-first taint (`--sink` + `--source external`); requires `discover --with-cfg`
  inspect       Inspect raw CFG / PDG / dominance for a function symbol
  metrics       Network & churn analytics (PageRank, betweenness, communities, git churn)
  semantic      Opt-in semantic search over function symbols (separate index artifact)
  communities   List or refresh named communities (analysis overlay)
  clones        Clone detection: exact Type-1 (`code_hash`), Type-2 Bloom LSH, or Type-3/4 SESE+1-WL fragments
  cpg           Hybrid CPG façade (topology + CFG/PDG archive)
  dead-code     Dead-code detection via graph reachability analysis

Security:
  vuln          OSV vulnerability triage / analyze
  deps          Dependency inventory match against OSV
  security      Security / OSV entrypoints (aliases of top-level `vuln`, `deps`, `taint`)

Policy:
  check         CI policy gateway
  review        Temporal PR analysis (`review paths` / `review check`)

Meta:
  export        Export graph or projections
  install       Install bundled agent pack (skills, optional policy)
  completions   Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell)
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Other:
  writeback     Lossless reconstruct / verify / patch Tier-1 sources from `.rgctl/` sidecars

events.text: How can a teammate explore this graph without cloning the repo?

Your teammate can explore the graph via **`rgctl serve`** — it launches an interactive dashboard and GraphQL API over HTTP:

```bash
rgctl serve
```

This starts a local web server (default `http://localhost:7000`) with:

- **Universe Dashboard** — visual graph of symbols, call paths, blast radius, communities
- **GraphQL API** — query the graph programmatically (`/graphql`)
- **Symbol search** — find classes, methods, by name/type
- **Call-path tracing** — see callers/callees for any symbol

**To expose to teammates remotely**, bind to `0.0.0.0`:

```bash
rgctl serve --bind 0.0.0.0:7000
```

Then share `http://<your-ip>:7000` with the team. They can:
- Browse the CoolStore architecture without cloning
- Inspect the changes from `test-pr2` (CartEndpoint, MDBs, Transformers)
- Run blast-radius queries on symbols
- Trace JMS message flow through OrderServiceMDB → CatalogService

The `.rgctl/` index is already built and committed, so the serve command reads the snapshot instantly — no rediscovery needed. Keep the terminal running while they explore.

## **Request**

```bash
rgctl semantic query "checkout" --format json
```

## **Response Summary**

The semantic search found 20 checkout-related functions ranked by relevance:

**Top matches (exact/best alignment):**

| Rank | Name | File | Score | Type |
|------|------|------|-------|------|
| 1 | `checkout` | `controllers.js:L?` | 0.50 | Frontend controller |
| 2 | `checkout` | `cart.js:L?` | 0.48 | Frontend service |
| 8 | `checkout` | `CartEndpoint.java` | **0.247** | **Backend JAX-RS endpoint** |

**Key finding:** The backend `CartEndpoint.checkout()` ranks 8th with score 0.247 — lower than the frontend functions because the semantic index captures behavioral patterns, not just naming. The frontend's cart service and controller functions have more "checkout-like" code semantics (state resets, clearing, navigation).

**Other related functions found:**
- `addToCart` (0.273) — frontend cart mutation
- `setCart` (0.288) — frontend state management  
- `reset` (0.300) — cleanup after checkout

**To inspect the backend checkout endpoint:**

```bash
rgctl relations CartEndpoint.checkout
```

This shows the call chain: `CartEndpoint.checkout()` → `ShoppingCartService.checkOutShoppingCart()` → `ShoppingCartOrderProcessor.process()` → JMS publish to `jms/topic/orders`.

The semantic API indexes function **semantics** (what code actually does), not just symbol names — useful for finding similar algorithms or related business logic across the codebase.

events.text: The dashboard looks stale after my edits. What should we do?

Run an **incremental graph update** to sync the dashboard with your edits:

```bash
rgctl update
```

This re-indexes only the **changed files** since the last discover — much faster than a full rebuild. It updates:
- Call-path edges you modified
- Symbol definitions
- Semantic embeddings (if you use `semantic query` again)

If you've made **major structural changes** (new packages, deleted classes), do a full rediscover instead:

```bash
rgctl discover .
```

Then you can browse the refreshed graph with:

```bash
rgctl serve --bind 0.0.0.0:7000
```

**What was stale:** The `.rgctl/` index was built against `origin/main` (see REVIEW_REPORT line 1). Your `test-pr2` branch edits weren't reflected in the graph until you run `update` or `discover`.

**Tip:** Use `rgctl watch` to auto-update on file saves during development:

```bash
rgctl watch
```

It debounces file events (default 25ms) and applies incremental updates so the dashboard stays fresh as you code.
